issues.title: Operator norm leaves the first argument unconstrained

failure_location.quote: The operator norm $\|L\|_{\mathcal L^i(X,Y)}:=\sup \left\{\left|L\left(h_1, \ldots, h_i\right)\right |_Y:\left|x_1\right|_X \leq 1, \ldots,\left|h_i\right|_X \leq 1\right\}, L\in \mathcal L^i(X,Y)$ makes these Banach spaces;  non separable when $X,Y$ are infinite-dimensional.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the displayed supremum is the operator norm. Literally, x_1 does not occur in L(h_1,\ldots,h_i), while h_1 has no unit-ball constraint. For any nonzero multilinear L, the remaining arguments can be normalized and h_1 can then be scaled to make the supremum infinite. The old proposition lemma:multilinear instead constrains every h_j and gives the finite operator norm.
issues.overall_effect: The introductory operator-norm definition is malformed, although the later formal proposition supplies the intended definition, so no formal-result chain is defeated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the first unit-ball condition |x_1|_X <= 1 in the introductory supremum by |h_1|_X <= 1, so that every argument h_1,...,h_i of L is constrained. No proof or downstream statement requires alteration.
issues.why_classification: The displayed arguments of L and the later proposition uniquely force h_1 in place of the unused x_1. This is a transcriptional variable mismatch; the formal development already uses the correct finite operator norm, so no mathematical inference needs repair.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: The operator norm $\|L\|_{\mathcal L^i(X,Y)}:=\sup \left\{\left|L\left(h^1, \ldots, h^i\right)\right |_Y:\left|h^1\right|_X = 1, \ldots,\left|h^i\right|_X = 1\right\}, L\in \mathcal L^i(X,Y)$ makes these Banach spaces;  non separable when $X,Y$ are infinite-dimensional.

issues.title: Codomain approximation property omitted from contribution summary

failure_location.quote: As we show in Theorem \ref{th:UAT_K_Banach}, UA is sharply achieved  in $C_B^k(X; Y)^{co}$, i.e. in $C_B^k(X,Y)$ compact-open topologies (see Definition \ref{def:compact_open_C2B}), via EDAs under only AP on $X$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $(X,|\cdot|_X),(Y,|\cdot|_Y)$ be  Banach spaces  with the Approximation Property, i.e. we are given $\left\{{\mathcal S}^X_\alpha\right\}_{\alpha \in A }\subset \mathcal L(X)$, $\left\{{\mathcal S}^Y_\beta\right\}_{\beta \in B }\subset \mathcal L(Y)$ satisfying Assumption \ref{ass:approx_pro}.
Since ${\mathcal S}^Y_\beta\xrightarrow{co} I$ (recall Assumption \ref{ass:approx_pro}), we can find $\beta \in B$ such that $I_{1}^{\beta,i}<\epsilon/3$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the compact-open UAT is established under AP only on X. The old theorem is stated under the immediately preceding setup in which both X and Y have AP, and the proof invokes ${\mathcal S}^Y_\beta\xrightarrow{co}I$ to approximate the output. Thus the old paper establishes the result under AP for X and Y, not under AP for X alone.
issues.overall_effect: The contribution summary overstates the scope of a main compact-open UAT; the formal theorem and proof remain valid under AP for both X and Y.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Revise the contribution summary to state that the compact-open UAT assumes the Approximation Property for both X and Y, rather than for X alone. The formal theorem and its proof can remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The X-only assertion is a coherent and strictly broader scope claim, while the proof genuinely invokes finite-rank approximation of the identity on Y. Adding AP on Y substantively narrows the advertised codomain class, so this is not a typo or a no-loss minor correction. Nevertheless, the same UAT, topology, method, and conclusion survive under the limited additional hypothesis without new proof architecture, making the issue moderate rather than serious.

issues.title: Exact rank-one derivative claim

failure_location.quote: e.g. exploiting that, in this case, $DF(x), D^2F(x)(h^1,\cdot) \in X^*$ have rank 1 (hence stronger UA is expected)

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We denote by $ X^*=\mathcal L(X,\mathbb R)$ the dual space.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose unconditionally claims exact rank one for DF(x) and D^2F(x)(h^1,\cdot). Since X*=\mathcal L(X,\mathbb R), such functionals have rank at most one. In particular, multilinearity gives D^2F(x)(0,\cdot)=0, of rank zero, and a constant F gives DF(x)=0. Only rank at most one—and hence finite rank—is unconditional.
issues.overall_effect: The local motivation incorrectly excludes zero derivatives, but its intended finite-rank observation and no formal theorem are affected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace “have rank 1” by “have rank at most one” (or, equivalently for the stated motivation, “have finite rank”). This preserves the finite-rank observation and requires no change to any formal result.
issues.why_classification: A functional in X* has rank one only when it is nonzero; constant F or h^1 = 0 gives rank zero. Accounting for this exceptional zero case is a short, routine local qualification, and the finite-rank motivation and all subsequent mathematics remain unchanged.
